description: Start here. Loaded datasets (id, name, path, loader config; live streams carry stream), the stream sources start_stream can start, time range, current time, your agent id and tabs, whether PlotJuggler has the user's focus and any dialog the user has open. A config's secrets (passwords, tokens) read as "<redacted>". rendering: how many times the main window drew in the last second (frames_last_s; floating docks not counted) and ms_since_last_frame (null before the first). While playing, frames_last_s near the display or playback rate means the window draws, 0 or 1 means it is stalled; whether the compositor shows those frames it cannot see.

description: Load a data file (MCAP, CSV, ULog, Parquet...). Returns when the import has finished, or after wait_s with a job_id while a large file still loads: its topics are readable as they arrive, job_wait returns the outcome and job_kill stops the import. By default the loader's own defaults apply (e.g. every topic). Returns the config the loader used, its secrets as "<redacted>"; a "<redacted>" passed back in config keeps the value this file was loaded with, only when the rest of config is that one unchanged (else pass the secret itself).

description: Create your own derived series with a Luau or Python script: for Python, or a script class that keeps state in its instance (create_derived_series takes a formula or a short Luau body; add_filter a built-in filter). Python: first line '# pj-script: python', one top-level class T (its id is set for you), @staticmethod create(params) returning T(), and calculate(self, time, value, *more_inputs); imports limited to math, cmath, statistics. A Luau script returns a class: return { name="X", create = function(params) local s = {}; return { calculate = function(t, v) ... return y end } end } (the id is set for you). t is seconds, v the input; keep state in the instance (integrators, bias removal). Several inputs are joined on equal timestamps (fields of one message always are; inputs that share none are refused): calculate(t, v, v1, v2, ...). Several outputs: pass `outputs` [names] and return that many numbers; they become topics <name>/<output>. Text (state labels such as "walking"): declare output="string" on the class (Luau table field or Python class attribute) and return strings; the user sees them in a State Transitions panel. Listed under Custom Topics, saved in layouts, untouched by the user's undo; the same name replaces it. Returns each output topic with its fields.

inputs.description: series paths as read_series takes them; a text series arrives as a string (value == "walking")

name.description: series name; your series of this name is replaced

outputs.description: output names, one number each from calculate (default: one output, `name`)

script.description: Luau or Python source, as above

Like add_script_series: listed under Custom Topics, removable with remove_script_series, outside the user's undo, the same name replaces it. Returns the output topic and field to plot.

filter.description: built-in filter id; an unknown one is refused with the list of available filters

input.description: series path, as read_series takes it

params.description: filter parameters; the ones left out take their defaults

description:
Read the settings of any dock, the user's included: plots, 3D and 2D scenes, Log panels, state strips. A dock's settings are the XML element a layout saves for it (a scene's camera, grid and each layer's point size, colour mode, colormap, range...; a plot's curves, colours, styles and axis ranges); set_widget_state changes them.
action 'list': every dock (id, tab, title, kind). 'get' (dock): its element as `xml`, and `options`: per element tag, each attribute the dock accepts with its type, allowed `values` or `min`/`max`, and `default` (the value an absent attribute takes); empty for a plugin's widget.

action.description: list: every dock; get: one dock's settings and options

dock.description: get: a dock id from list

name: widget_state
title: Read dock settings

description: Replace a dock's settings (widget_state reads them) with your XML element: get it right before, change attributes, send the whole element back with the same root tag; keep what you do not change as get returned it (it holds the camera and the view: an older get moves them back). A refused element leaves the dock as it was, and the error names the attribute and what it accepts; an attribute not in options, or a series or topic that is not loaded, is refused too; a dock whose get lists no options (a plugin's widget) takes any element, unchecked. Each call is one undo step for the user. Returns the dock's element as applied.

dock.description: a dock id from widget_state list

name: set_widget_state
title: Change dock settings

description: The whole workspace as layout XML, as File > Save Layout writes it: every tab (the user's and yours), plots, scenes, derived series and markers. Without path it returns xml: generic unless bind_sources, which records the loaded files and streams with absolute paths; every setting's secrets (a plugin's, a widget's, a derived series' parameters) read as "<redacted>".

bind_sources.description: record the loaded files and running streams so the layout reloads them (default: true with path, as the menu; false for text); false: curves bind by topic and field to whatever is loaded

description: Replace the whole workspace (the user's tabs too) with a layout, as File > Load Layout does: pass xml (the text), path (a layout file) or url (http/https; only the layout is downloaded). Data paths in text or from a url must be absolute; a relative one is reported, never guessed. The files and streams it names load when not loaded already, without asking. If the workspace holds anything (a plot, a derived series, an open toolbox, undo history), the user is asked to confirm first (a job_id after wait_s while they decide; job_kill withdraws the question or stops the download, but a layout already applying completes). Refused while another layout load runs, and for a secret still reading "<redacted>" (load the file save_layout wrote with path, or put the real values in). Your tabs and series in it come back as yours. Returns loaded and the app's warnings (missing data, a relative path, a newer format), or its error.

description:
Read summary statistics ('stats'), a min/max-preserving downsample ('buckets'), or up to 200 raw samples inside a mandatory window ('raw'). Non-finite values are 'invalid', excluded from min/max/mean/stddev. buckets are columnar (t0, dt, n, min, max, mean; t_i = t0 + i*dt, or 't' when irregular). Stats carry 't_start_display_s' when playback is bound, so bucket i's display time = t_start_display_s + t0 + i*dt.
'paths' is an ARRAY: ask several at once. A bad path returns as an error beside the ones that worked. A topic path (no field) reads all its numeric fields. buckets take up to 8 paths; raw takes 4. t_start_s/t_end_s (display axis) narrow the read and re-base t; raw REQUIRES both.

paths.description: topic/field paths; a bare string is accepted for a single series

name: read_series
title: Read series

description: Wait for a live series to cross a threshold: returns the first sample that ARRIVES AFTER this call and satisfies 'comparison' against 'threshold' (its value and display time), or fails after 'timeout_s'. For watching a stream; samples already loaded do not count (read_series finds those).

threshold.description: the value to compare each new sample with

wait_s.description: seconds to wait for the result. A call still running then returns {job_id, state, progress} and carries on in the background: job_wait gets its result, job_kill stops it. 0 returns the job_id at once.

name: wait_for
title: Wait for a live value

description: Run a Luau computation and get the answer back — nothing is created or shown. Picked automatically: SCALAR (default) takes the same inputs/expression/body/global as create_derived_series and returns stats, add 'buckets' for the shape. OBJECT form kicks in when an input is an object topic or 'at_s'/'window' is given: requires 'body' (reads inputs["<topic>"], returns a table of 'outputs') and 'outputs' (["name:type", …], type is 'number', 'string', or a builtin object type e.g. 'kPointCloud'); 'at_s' evaluates at one display-seconds instant, 'window':{start_s,end_s} over a span, neither defaults to the playhead. Objects come back only as summaries, never bytes. To keep a result, create_derived_object.

body.description: scalar: return ...; object: reads inputs[..], returns table

wait_s.description: seconds to wait for the result. A call still running then returns {job_id, state, progress} and carries on in the background: job_wait gets its result, job_kill stops it. 0 returns the job_id at once.

name: evaluate
title: Evaluate a computation

description: Create a derived timeseries computed live from its inputs. Each sample sees 'value' (first input), 'v1'..'vN' (further inputs, in order), and 'time' (seconds). Use 'expression' for a stateless formula ('value * 2'); for stateful transforms like a derivative, use 'global' (runs once, persistent locals) + 'body' (statements ending in return; no value suppresses the sample). For Python or a script class: add_script_series; a built-in filter: add_filter (where listed). Saved in layouts. Reports whether undo protection held.

body.description: Luau statements ending in return (overrides expression)

global.description: Luau run once; its locals persist across samples

inputs.description: topic/field paths; a text series arrives as a string (value == "walking")

outputs.description: OPTIONAL — several series from ONE node (default: just 'name'). The body then returns one value per output, in order: outputs ['roll','pitch','yaw'] with a body ending 'return r, p, y'.

name: create_derived_series
title: Create a derived series

description: Install a live on-demand computation over object topics (point clouds, scene entities...) — evaluated on request, not eagerly per sample like create_derived_series. 'body' reads inputs["<topic>"] and returns a table of the declared 'outputs' (["name:type", …]). Without 'pin_at_s' it stays live for a later consumer (e.g. scene_view) to query; with 'pin_at_s' it is a FINDING, evaluated once at that display-seconds instant and kept (shown under <plugin>/<name>/…). Either way this call also evaluates it once itself and returns that first bundle. Saved in layouts. Undo protection is verified when supported; failure is reported.

pin_at_s.description: OPTIONAL — pin as a finding, display seconds

wait_s.description: seconds to wait for the result. A call still running then returns {job_id, state, progress} and carries on in the background: job_wait gets its result, job_kill stops it. 0 returns the job_id at once.

name: create_derived_object
title: Create a derived object

description:
Create plot markers from a Luau rule you write (preferred), or from a simple threshold template. There is ONE marker set of yours: calling this again REPLACES it (use remove_markers to clear it). Saved in layouts.
RAW FORM: 'inputs' (series the rule reads) + 'rule' (a Luau script, run once over the full series) + optional 'output' (series path the markers attach to; default = first input; "__global__" renders on every plot, only for events meaningful against ANY signal).
Write rules with when(series, condition), not loops:
  when("/speed", above(2)):backgroundColor("red", {label="fast"}) -- shade while true
  when("/acc", outside(-3, 3)):event({label="overload", minGap=1}) -- point where it starts
  when("/mode", changes()):verticalLine({label=function(v, prev) return prev.."->"..v end})
  when("/mode"):backgroundColor({[0]="gray", [1]="green"}) -- by value; or a function
Conditions: above, below, between(a,b), outside(a,b), equals, isTrue(), changes(), or function(v, t, prev, prev_t) -> bool (t int64 ns; other series: s:atTime(t)). Marks fire once per stretch (every=true: per sample); minDuration / minGap (s) drop short regions / close marks: use them on raw high-rate (IMU) signals; cross-check a slower signal. The reply counts markers: past ~50 the rule is wrong.
Loops only for windows/state: series("topic/field") -> s:size(), s:at(i) 0-based {t, v}, s:atTime(t); startMarker(t) / closeMarker(t, opts); createVerticalMarker(t, opts), createPointMarker(t, y, opts), createHorizontalMarker(y, opts), createBandMarker(lo, hi, opts); bandPower(s, f_lo_hz, f_hi_hz); GetSeriesNames().
opts: label, description, category, color ("#RRGGBB"|Qt name), severity ("info"|"warning"|"error"|"critical"), status.
TEMPLATE FORM (writes a when() rule): 'series', 'comparison', 'threshold', optional 'label' and 'style'.

inputs.description: topic/field paths the rule reads (raw form)

output.description: raw form: where the markers render, as above

style.description: template form; line: a mark per matching sample

title: Remove a derived series

description: Drive the transport: the time cursor, shared by every plot. action: 'state' (read it), 'play', 'pause', 'seek' (to 'time_s'), 'rate' (to 'rate'; 1.0 = real time). Every call returns the whole state - playing, current_time_s, range {min_s, max_s}, rate - so a clamped seek shows where the cursor actually landed. Times are DISPLAY-AXIS SECONDS, the numbers on the plot X axes: a feature found in read_series buckets sits at stats.t_start_display_s + bucket.t.
name: playback
title: Playback

description:
Compose plot tabs of your own. A tab you create is marked with your ownership badge and is the only place you may draw: the user's tabs are not yours to fill, zoom or close, and they do not go away when you close yours. Your tabs are saved with the layout and stay out of the user's undo/redo.
action: 'create' (optional 'tab' name and 'title') | 'add'/'remove' ('curves', topic/field paths) | 'zoom' ('start_s'..'end_s' display-axis seconds; omit both to fit) | 'focus' (bring it forward, e.g. before a screenshot) | 'close' | 'list'. Every action answers with the tab as the host holds it, so a curve that did not land shows as missing instead of being reported as drawn. A series you made with create_derived_series is addressable here as 'name/value'.

title.description: tab title shown to the user (create)

name: plot_tab
title: Your plot tabs

description:
Open 3D/2D scene views of your own, the counterpart of plot_tab: same watermark and ownership, the user's scene docks unreachable.
action: 'create' (optional 'view', 'kind' "3d"|"2d" default "3d", 'title') | 'attach'/'detach' ('topics', object-topic paths) | 'focus' | 'close' | 'list'. Every action reads back what the view actually holds, so a topic that did not land shows as missing instead of attached.

title.description: view title shown to the user (create)

name: scene_view
title: Your scene views

description: Your calls still running in the background, and those that ended in the last minutes: job_id, tool, summary, state (running, waiting_for_user, completed, failed, killed), elapsed_s, progress.
name: jobs_list
title: List your jobs

description: Wait for a background job: returns its result once it ends (again on every call, until it expires minutes later), or its job_id, state and progress if it is still running after timeout_s.

job_id.description: a job_id a long call returned

name: job_wait
title: Wait for a job

description: Stop a background job: an evaluation stops computing, a file import stops (a stopped reload always restores the data it was replacing), a stream stops (its data stays), an export writes nothing, and a dialog the job opened for the user closes. Returns its final state: killed, or completed/failed if it ended first; when the stop takes longer to act, its state with stopping=true (job_wait then returns when it has ended).

job_id.description: a job_id a long call returned

name: job_kill
